references.text: Prohibition against false weights and measures in Leviticus, establishing the same principle of justice in trade as Deuteronomy 25:14.
Proverbs condemns a false weight as an abomination to the Lord, affirming the moral principle of honest dealing.
Proverbs mentions both false weights and false measures as detestable to the Lord, directly related to the prohibition against differing standards.
Proverbs repeats that a dishonest weight is an abomination to the Lord, and false scales are not good.
The prophet Micah condemns unjust measures and false weights as something the Lord cannot tolerate.
Ezekiel commands that Israel shall have a just weight, a just ephah, and a just bath.
